summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type II diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, and heart failure was admitted for evaluation of a nonhealing foot ulcer following a prior toe amputation. He underwent a right lower extremity angiogram to assess blood flow, which showed arterial blockages but sufficient perfusion for healing. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout the admission. On postoperative day one, he developed hyperkalemia with a potassium rise from 5.5 to 6.5, prompting an urgent two-hour hemodialysis session with a low-potassium bath. His lisinopril was discontinued and amlodipine increased per nephrology guidance. He was discharged home on day two in stable condition with medication adjustments, wound care instructions, and follow-up arranged with vascular surgery.
problems: Ulcer of other part of foot
Amputation of limb(s) causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
